examples.trans: The chef says that this is a very unreliable choice.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'the people' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Такой уж ненадёжный народ эти девочки.
examples.trans: Girls are such unreliable people.

examples.text: Народ меня поддерживает.
examples.trans: The people support me.

examples.text: Здесь много народу.
examples.trans: There are a lot of people here.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'these', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Это я соврал, чтобы уйти пораньше.
examples.trans: I made that up so I could leave early.

examples.text: Да, это время нам отлично подходит.
examples.trans: Yes, that time suits us very well.

examples.text: Это мой очень близкий друг.
examples.trans: He is my very close friend.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'nothing', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ничего, мы вдвоём с тобой отлично посидим!
examples.trans: That is fine, the two of us will have a great time together!

examples.text: Ничего страшного, я сейчас коробку распакую.
examples.trans: No big deal, I will unpack a box right now.

examples.text: Пожалуйста, ничего больше мне сейчас не говори.
examples.trans: Please do not say anything more to me right now.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'with / from', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Любимый мужчина готовит мне вкусный ужин.
examples.trans: My beloved man is cooking me a delicious dinner.

examples.text: Смотри, твой су-шеф сейчас звонит.
examples.trans: Look, your sous-chef is calling right now.

examples.text: Поставь телефон на громкую связь.
examples.trans: Put the phone on speakerphone.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Лёва, какую ерунду ты сейчас говоришь?
examples.trans: Lyova, what nonsense are you talking right now?

examples.text: Ты обязательно пройдёшь полное обследование.
examples.trans: You will definitely undergo a full medical checkup.

examples.text: Ты уже закончил работу, Лёва?
examples.trans: Have you finished work already, Lyova?

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'лично'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Да, это время нам отлично подходит.
examples.trans: Yes, that time suits us very well.

examples.text: Отлично, тогда до встречи вечером!
examples.trans: Great, then see you in the evening!

examples.text: Ничего, мы вдвоём с тобой отлично посидим!
examples.trans: That is fine, the two of us will have a great time together!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'сидеть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'sit a while', paired with 'сидеть'.

examples.text: Катя, мы с девочками хотели вечером посидеть.
examples.trans: Katya, the girls and I wanted to hang out tonight.

examples.text: Вообще-то мы хотели спокойно посидеть девочками.
examples.trans: Actually we wanted to sit quietly with the girls.

examples.text: Мы хотели посидеть в женской компании.
examples.trans: We wanted to sit in female company.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Ладно, давай закажем себе по коктейлю.
examples.trans: Alright, let us order ourselves a cocktail each.

examples.text: Ладно, я тогда пойду, не буду мешать.
examples.trans: Alright, I will go then, I will not bother you.

examples.text: Да ладно, Костя, я совсем не против.
examples.trans: Come on, Kostya, I do not mind at all.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'come on', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

related.gloss: to give (the verb it comes from)

examples.text: Настя, давай не будем лезть в чужую жизнь.
examples.trans: Nastya, let us stay out of other people's lives.

examples.text: Ну хорошо, давай попробуем это сделать.
examples.trans: Well alright, let us try to do that.

examples.text: Ладно, давай закажем себе по коктейлю.
examples.trans: Alright, let us order ourselves a cocktail each.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will order', paired with 'заказывать'.

examples.text: Может, закажем?
examples.trans: Maybe we should order?

examples.text: Мы заказали чай и бутерброды.
examples.trans: We ordered tea and sandwiches.

examples.text: Если опоздают, пицца бесплатно. Может, закажем?
examples.trans: If they're late, the pizza is free. Maybe we should order?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to oneself', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я просто медицинскую книжку себе продлевал.
examples.trans: I was simply renewing my medical book.

examples.text: Ладно, давай закажем себе по коктейлю.
examples.trans: Alright, let us order ourselves a cocktail each.

examples.text: Возьми его себе, я пока не хочу.
examples.trans: Take it for yourself, I do not want it yet.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'according to', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Тем более я гениальный шеф-повар.
examples.trans: Especially since I am a brilliant head chef.

examples.text: Поставь телефон на громкую связь.
examples.trans: Put the phone on speakerphone.

examples.text: Вы лучше спокойно дома отдохните.
examples.trans: You had better rest quietly at home.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'cocktail' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Ладно, давай закажем себе по коктейлю.
examples.trans: Alright, let us order ourselves a cocktail each.

examples.text: Я сделаю тебе свой фирменный коктейль.
examples.trans: I will make you my signature cocktail.

examples.text: Что это за интересный коктейль такой?
examples.trans: What kind of interesting cocktail is that?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.text: Смотри, твой су-шеф сейчас звонит.
examples.trans: Look, your sous-chef is calling right now.

examples.text: Лёва, какую ерунду ты сейчас говоришь?
examples.trans: Lyova, what nonsense are you talking right now?

examples.text: Ей сейчас очень плохо после этой истории.
examples.trans: She feels awful right now after that whole story.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'питок'). Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'drinks' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Сейчас Костя сделает нам напитки.
examples.trans: Kostya will make us drinks right now.

examples.text: Холодный напиток.
examples.trans: A cold drink.

examples.text: Ты совсем не пьёшь крепкие напитки?
examples.trans: Do you not drink strong drinks at all?
